GZ Analytics (customer): Hey team — after we pinned our model via the console to a specific variant, our embeddings length jumped from 1024 -> 1536 and our vector DB indexing failed. No API errors, just different vector size. Example request_id: abc123def. Can you check?

Maria (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body/headers you used and confirm the model name + whether you used the 'pin to variant' flow in the Console? Also earliest time this started.

GZ Analytics (customer): Sure. We pinned from the Console on 2026-03-15 at ~11:02 UTC (variant lock id: variant-lock-20260315). Sample curl we used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embedding-1","input":["test doc"], "metadata": {"customer":"gz"}}'
```Response (truncated):```json
{"request_id":"abc123def","model":"rwd-embedding-1","embedding":[0.001, ... , 1536 values total]}
```We didn't set any explicit variant header; Console shows pinned variant alias "blue-2026".

Brian (devx): Thanks — two quick possibilities: 1) The pinned alias could be resolving to a different variant (e.g. a quantized variant with a different output dim), or 2) there's a mapping/cache issue in the variant resolver after the rollout. Can you share the request_id and the exact model id from the Console (not the alias)?

GZ Analytics (customer): Console model id is "rwd-embedding-1@blue-2026" and request_id abc123def. Happened for ~50 calls across a short window, then continued until now.

Zoe (eng-oncall): I'm looking at the routing logs for request_id=abc123def and time window 2026-03-15T11:02:10Z. The variant-resolver returned a fallback: "rwd-embed-quant-1536" due to a metadata mismatch in the alias mapping. That variant has a 1536 vector size (we recently onboarded a quantized variant for internal perf testing) — the alias should have resolved to "rwd-embed-1024-fp". Root cause: when the alias update during the canary->prod rollout overlapped with a variant cache refresh, an old mapping was briefly re-added to the alias table.

Terra (ops): Immediate mitigation applied: updated alias mapping to point explicitly to rwd-embed-1024-fp and triggered a variant-map cache refresh:```bash
POST /internal/variant-map/refresh
{ "alias": "blue-2026" }
```Also rolled back the canary mapping that referenced the quantized variant. Flushed edge caches.

GZ Analytics (customer): Re-ran the same request — now receiving 1024-length vectors. Looks good. Thank you! :white_check_mark:

Maria (support): Great to hear. We'll open an internal incident for the alias race condition and follow up with a postmortem. ACTIONS: create incident RINF-8421, add guardrail to block alias pointing to variants with mismatched embedding sizes for the same model family, add regression test for pinned variants during rollouts, and notify customers who pinned between 2026-03-15T11:00 and 11:10 UTC.

Zoe (eng-oncall): Adding notes: monitor for 24h, we pushed a small fix to alias write path to avoid re-adding stale mappings during concurrent rollouts (PR #4682). We'll also add a startup check that verifies embedding dimensionality compatibility when aliasing variants.

Maria (support): I'll follow up with the customer via email with the incident ticket and remediation timeline. Thanks everyone.

GZ Analytics (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please CC me on the incident.

Brian (devx): For future repros, you can run this repro command to assert vector size explicitly:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embedding-1@blue-2026","input":["ping" ] }' | jq '.embedding | length'
```That prints the embedding length so customers and SRE can quickly validate.

Zoe (eng-oncall): I'll add that check to the canary runbook as well. :eyes:
